description: President announces a ban on exports of cooking oil and its raw materials from 28 April 2022
premise: An export ban is an adverse policy shock for Indonesian palm oil producers.

description: President announces that palm oil exports reopen on 23 May 2022
premise: Lifting the export ban is a favourable policy shock for palm oil producers.

description: Finance minister announces the palm oil export levy is cut to zero until 31 August 2022 (PMK 115/2022)
premise: Removing the export levy is a favourable policy shock for palm oil producers.

description: NasDem declares Anies Baswedan its 2024 presidential candidate while a member of the governing coalition
premise: A governing-coalition party nominates a candidate seen as opposed to the sitting president's camp. The tested firms are those tied to that party.

description: Analog terrestrial television switched off in Greater Jakarta; two private groups' stations comply a day late
premise: The analog switch-off is an adverse policy shock for incumbent free-to-air broadcasters.

description: Golkar and PAN declare support for Prabowo Subianto's presidential bid
premise: A governing-coalition party joins the presidential candidate who then led the polls and was backed by the largest bloc of governing parties. The tested firms are those tied to that party.

description: Presidential Regulation 32/2024 on publisher rights announced at National Press Day
premise: A rule obliging digital platforms to deal with news publishers is a favourable policy shock for media groups.

description: Airlangga Hartarto announces his resignation as Golkar chair
premise: The chair of a governing-coalition party resigns suddenly two months before a new president takes office; his expected successor is close to the incoming president. The tested firms are those tied to that party.

description: Perindo declares it joins the Prabowo-Gibran coalition
premise: A party that backed a losing presidential candidate joins the coalition of the president-elect. The tested firms are those tied to that party.

description: European Commission proposes a 12-month delay of the EU Deforestation Regulation
premise: The European Commission proposes delaying an EU import rule that affects palm oil. The question is whether ties to the Indonesian government change how much a firm gains.

description: Prabowo Subianto inaugurated; Red and White Cabinet announced that evening
premise: The new president takes office and announces a broad cabinet that keeps the governing-coalition parties in government.

description: The first Danantara launch, set for 7 November 2024, is called off the evening before
premise: The launch of a new state fund that would take over the state's shares in listed SOEs is postponed without a new date. The project owner's registered view is that the fund's creation is a governance cost for minority shareholders of state-owned firms.

description: President announces that Danantara will be launched on 24 February 2025
premise: The president announces a firm launch date for the state fund, after an earlier postponement. The project owner's registered view is that the fund's creation is a governance cost for minority shareholders of state-owned firms.

description: Danantara launched; Law 1/2025, Government Regulation 10/2025 and the decree appointing its leadership signed the same day
premise: The state fund is launched and takes over dividend rights and control of the state's shares in listed SOEs from the Finance Ministry, with less parliamentary oversight.

description: Government decides to form village cooperatives (Koperasi Desa Merah Putih) to be financed by the state banks
premise: The government decides on a nationwide village-cooperative programme and names the state banks as its lenders.

description: The state's Series B shares in Mandiri, BRI, BNI and BTN are transferred to Danantara's operating holding (deed of 2025-03-22, disclosed 2025-03-24)
premise: The state's shares in the four listed state banks are legally transferred to the state fund's operating holding, as the law passed the month before required.

description: Export levy on crude palm oil raised to 10 percent from 17 May 2025 (PMK 30/2025)
premise: A higher export levy is an adverse policy shock for palm oil producers.

description: The forest-area task force hands 394,547 ha of seized plantations to state firm Agrinas Palma Nusantara
premise: The state seizes a large area of plantations from private companies and hands it to a state firm; enforcement of this kind is an adverse shock for private plantation groups.

description: Constitutional Court ruling 21/PUU-XXIII/2025 states in its reasoning that the ban on concurrent posts also covers deputy ministers
premise: The Constitutional Court signals that deputy ministers may not also sit as commissioners. The tested firms are those with sitting government officials on their boards.

description: Constitutional Court ruling 128/PUU-XXIII/2025 bars deputy ministers from serving as SOE commissioners, with a two-year transition
premise: The Constitutional Court bars deputy ministers from sitting as SOE commissioners, with two years to comply. The tested firms are those with sitting government officials on their boards.

description: Cabinet reshuffle replaces the finance minister and four other ministers
premise: The president replaces a long-serving finance minister and four other ministers.

description: Finance minister announces that about Rp200 trillion of state cash will be placed in the state banks
premise: The finance minister announces that a large amount of government cash will be deposited with the five state banks and with no other bank.

description: Erick Thohir moved from Minister of SOEs to Minister of Youth and Sports; the SOE post is left vacant
premise: A minister who founded a listed media group is moved from the SOE portfolio to the Youth and Sports portfolio and stays in cabinet. The tested firms are those whose owner holds office or a party role.

description: DPR committee and government agree a bill that turns the Ministry of SOEs into an agency (BP BUMN)
premise: Parliament and the government agree to replace the Ministry of SOEs with a regulatory agency that sits beside the state fund.
